key_insight: Post-training quantization works because pretrained models develop error-canceling hidden-state dynamics and an output layer geometry that preserves the most important token predictions.
engineering_relevance: This means large language models can often be compressed to lower precision with little performance loss, enabling cheaper storage, faster inference, and lower memory bandwidth.
method: Compare full-precision vs. quantized forward passes in pretrained and randomly initialized models
Measure how layerwise quantization errors accumulate through depth
Analyze LM-head geometry to see which token scores and probabilities remain stable
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the authors validate these mechanisms across multiple models and quantization settings, showing much slower hidden-error growth in pretrained quantized models than in random ones.
watch_item: The effect depends on pretrained residual interactions and output-layer behavior, so extreme bit-width reduction or different model architectures may not preserve the same robustness.
